title: feat(verify): tests come from a separate oracle session

catches.what: provenance step: a pull_request checkout has no origin/<base> ref, so git rev-list failed (red from 8b1b6ff to f8226b9). CI wiring, not reachable by unit tests.
provenance step: fetch-depth `pull_request && 0 || 1` evaluates to 1 because 0 is falsy, so the checkout had no history. Hidden behind the first bug.
ledger draft counted one bug once per failing commit (4 catches for 2 bugs); found by reading the first real draft. The oracle's tests pinned the wrong rule because the brief stated it.

d326c34 deleted programmaticCosts and the Run type from scripts/ledger.ts along with the old catch rule; the kept cost tests fail (programmaticCosts is not a function) and `pnpm ledger draft` would crash calling it.

notes: Implementer (main session) cost not measured. The oracle ran Stryker unprompted and added one test for a gap it found; no code bug.
human: Trailer whitespace: should "Verified-by: oracle  " or a CRLF line count? The implementation trims and accepts it; untested.
timed_out, startup_failure, action_required and neutral conclusions: neither failure nor success under the catch rule, so they neither start nor end a streak. The brief is silent.

A cancelled, skipped or missing run between a failing commit and a passing one (e.g. PR #37 a1cb760, where every check was cancelled): does it break the streak? The implementation keeps the streak going; untested.

A failing commit followed by a commit that fails and then passes on a re-run: the re-run commit counts as passing, so the earlier failure counts as a catch, though arguably only a re-run fixed it. Untested.

One catch per streak cannot split two bugs that fail back to back: PR #37 had two (missing origin/<base>, then falsy fetch-depth) in one streak, and the draft gives one catch. The hand-entered checks@e32ecae catch is the human record of the second.

Hook bypasses: the guard matches command text, so git -C <dir> commit, git aliases, a commit run inside a script, or a merge through gh api / the web UI are not caught. CI provenance is the backstop for commits; nothing backstops merges outside gh pr merge except branch protection.
